subject: Dedicated/private VPC: operational isolation asks & evidence matrix
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated/private VPC: operational isolation asks & evidence matrix

Hi Alicia,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the clear overview of ClearBridge's isolation needs for PHI processing and cross-tenant separation. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can align on whether Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) is the right fit: 

Key constraints you emphasized:
- Data residency: production inference must run inside your AWS account in us-east-1 (control plane can be Redwood or customer-managed).
- Strict separation of customer data and images; no multi-tenant compute or disk sharing.
- KM requirements: customer-managed keys with HSM/KMS integration and auditability.
- Evidence needed for procurement: architecture diagram, SOC2 artifacts, keystore integration notes, and network firewall/IP ranges.

How we see the options mapping to your asks: 
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding but control plane and model artifacts live in Redwood-managed environment; not suitable unless you accept egress and key custody tradeoffs.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools in Redwood infra with logical tenancy. Good for performance and single-tenant compute, but requires discussion about control plane placement and whether we can provide customer VPC peering and customer KMS.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full customer VPC deployment or on-prem package; best for your requirement to host inference within your AWS account and to own KMS/HSM keys.

Requested deliverables from Redwood for your procurement team:
1) Short architecture diagram showing Dedicated vs Private VPC deployment variants and where keys live.
2) Evidence bundle: SOC2 summary, TLS cert rotation notes, and audit log snapshot example.
3) Integration matrix for KMS approaches (customer-managed KMS in customer account, BYOK flows, HSM).
4) Checklist of network requirements (CIDR, ports, peering, NAT/GW expectations).

I looped in Karthik to answer the KMS and networking specifics and Jordan for commercial/timeline coordination. Proposed next steps:
- Karthik to send a short technical note + attachments with the KMS matrix and a draft diagram by tomorrow EOD.
- Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra lead the week of June 16 to validate control plane and KMS options.
- I'll prepare the procurement evidence bundle and a one-page comparison table for your legal team.

Any corrections to the recap are welcome. If this looks right, Alicia, can you confirm which dates work for the deep dive and whether procurement needs a PO or an NDA before we share the SOC2 summary?

Best,
Marcus

Marcus — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications and asks from procurement/infra: 

1) Control plane residency: our security team insists that the inference compute must be launched in our account (dedicated or private) and that model artifacts cannot be stored on shared S3 buckets managed by a third party. Is 'Dedicated capacity' an option where Redwood provisions GPUs into our account (customer-owned VPC)? If not, we need the private deployment option details.

2) KMS: we want to use our AWS KMS CMKs with key usage logs retained for 24 months. Can Redwood confirm support for using customer-managed CMKs for model encryption at rest and for signing? If there are limitations with the Dedicated model, call them out.

3) Evidence: procurement can accept SOC2 summary and network diagram. For SOC2 we need dates (most recent audit) and an engagement letter or point of contact.

4) Timeline: target POC in Q3, pilot in Q4 pending procurement. For the deep-dive, June 17 or 18 afternoon ET works for our infra lead.

Small ask: please include a brief note on what parts of the control plane will still be accessible to Redwood engineers for monitoring/support in each deployment mode.

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Rivera
Director, IT Infrastructure | ClearBridge Health

Alicia — quick technical answers inline to help procurement: 

1) Dedicated capacity in-customer-account: we offer a VPC-hosted Dedicated option where compute nodes (GPU instances) and block storage are deployed into the customer's AWS account through an IAM cross-account provisioning flow. In that variant, model artifacts can be stored in customer-owned S3 with bucket policies restricted to the compute role. The control plane (for billing/rollouts) can remain Redwood-managed but optional control plane components can be deployed as light-weight collectors inside the customer VPC if you require.

2) KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed AWS KMS CMKs for data-at-rest encryption. Our recommended pattern is envelope encryption where the root keys remain in your KMS and Redwood only sees encrypted CEKs. We can support HSM-backed keys if you supply the HSM-compatible interface. Logs: we can provide guidance on CloudTrail events to capture key usage; retention policy is controlled by your account.

3) Evidence: Redwood's SOC2 Type II report is available with redactions; we can share a cover letter and an auditor contact under an NDA. The report's most recent audit period ended 2024-12-31.

4) Support/access: for Dedicated-in-customer-account the default is that Redwood engineers do not have persistent SSH or console access to instances. We provide an agent that collects telemetry and an ops API with scoped roles; for escalations we can request temporary access with customer approval and full audit logs. For Private on-prem installs, support access is negotiated and normally uses a temporary access token and jump host under your control.

I attached the KMS matrix and a short diagram to illustrate both variants. Happy to walk through these in the deep dive.

- Karthik
